questions.stem: A patient with leukaemia (blood cancer) receives a bone marrow transplant. Why does this treatment work?

options.text: Bone marrow contains antibiotics that kill cancer cells
Bone marrow contains stem cells that can differentiate into healthy blood cells
Bone marrow replaces the patient's entire immune system instantly
Bone marrow provides nutrients that the blood cells need

questions.explanation: Bone marrow contains adult stem cells that can differentiate into all types of blood cells (red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets). After destroying the cancerous bone marrow, the transplanted stem cells can produce new, healthy blood cells.

questions.stem: Embryonic stem cells can differentiate into any cell type, but adult stem cells can only differentiate into a limited range. What is the term for the ability of embryonic stem cells?

options.text: Mitosis
Specialisation
Pluripotency
Mutation

questions.explanation: Pluripotency is the ability of a stem cell to differentiate into almost any cell type in the body. Embryonic stem cells are pluripotent, while adult stem cells are multipotent (can only become a limited range of cell types). This is why embryonic stem cells have greater potential for treating a wider range of diseases.

questions.stem: Some people object to embryonic stem cell research on ethical grounds. Which is a valid ethical concern?

options.text: Embryonic stem cells always cause cancer
The embryo is destroyed in the process, which some consider destruction of a potential human life
Embryonic stem cells cannot treat any diseases
Adult stem cells are always better than embryonic stem cells

questions.explanation: The main ethical concern is that obtaining embryonic stem cells requires the destruction of an embryo, which some people believe represents the beginning of a human life. This is a genuine ethical debate -- it does not mean the research is without medical value, but rather that the source of the cells raises moral questions.

questions.stem: Scientists are researching using stem cells to grow new nerve cells for patients with spinal cord injuries. Why is this considered a potential breakthrough?

options.text: Nerve cells normally divide rapidly and can repair themselves
Mature nerve cells cannot divide, so stem cells offer a way to replace damaged ones
Stem cells from the spinal cord are easy to extract
Nerve cells are the simplest type of specialised cell

questions.explanation: Once nerve cells (neurones) are fully differentiated, they generally cannot divide to replace damaged cells. This is why spinal cord injuries often cause permanent paralysis. Stem cells could potentially be directed to differentiate into new nerve cells, offering hope of restoring function.

questions.stem: In plants, meristem tissue contains stem cells that allow growth throughout the plant's life. A gardener takes a cutting from a plant and it grows roots. What does this demonstrate?

options.text: Plant cells can only grow in soil
Plant stem cells in the meristem can differentiate into new root cells
The cutting contains seeds that germinate
All plant cells are stem cells

questions.explanation: Plant meristem cells retain the ability to differentiate into any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life. When a cutting is taken, meristem cells can differentiate into root cells, allowing the cutting to develop a new root system. This is why plants can be cloned from cuttings.
